issue: Under U.S.S.G. § 2B1.1 cmt. n.3(F)(i), may a court apply the $500-per-access-device loss floor to each unauthorized credit card a defendant possessed, or is that per-card multiplier an impermissible reading of the Guidelines under Stinson and Kisor?

sides.position: The $500 per-access-device multiplier in § 2B1.1 cmt. n.3(F)(i) is invalid or cannot be applied per card, because the commentary conflicts with the guideline and does not bind the court under Stinson and Kisor.
cases: United States v. Kirilyuk, No. 19-10447 (9th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: The $500 per-access-device multiplier applies to all unauthorized access devices a defendant possesses, and the commentary is an authoritative interpretation to be followed.
cases: United States v. Moore, 788 F.3d 693 (7th Cir. 2015)

quote: In invalidating the multiplier, the majority badly misapplies Stinson, creates a lopsided split with our sister circuits, and embraces an anomalous concurring opinion from a Sixth Circuit case that involved critically different facts.
cite: United States v. Ruslan Kirilyuk, No. 19-10447 (9th Cir. 2022)
